items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Aretha Franklin, I don’t know what she made, but you know what happened with her— everything she made was a hit.

ctx.x: Well, no. See, he had a great band. He had Ronnie Cuber... He had a great band himself. That told me right there that John Hammond didn’t know the first thing about talent. Because he wouldn’t know it, and the people listening to this or reading this are going to be surprised, because John Hammond fired George Benson (I mean, not fired him—let him go), Aretha Franklin, and Eddie Harris, and the next record each one of them made, you know what happened? A hit record. The next record they made, a hit record. Eddie…

Aretha Franklin, I don’t know what she made, but you know what happened with her— everything she made was a hit. And George, the next record he made with me, which was a hit, and then he went on to CTI, started singing, and that was a hit. John Hammond missed all three of those people. They were right on the label.
You were touring with them in ‘67, ‘68, ‘69...
